q1: How do I check a laptop's warranty by serial number?
a1: Pick the brand, paste the serial number and press Check. For Lenovo and ThinkPad laptops you instantly see whether the warranty is active, the exact end date, every coverage line, and the build, ship and purchase dates.
q2: Where do I find my laptop's serial number?
a2: It is on the sticker underneath the laptop (S/N, Serial or Service Tag). On Windows, run (Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS).SerialNumber in PowerShell. On Linux, run sudo cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial. On a Mac, open Apple menu → About This Mac.
q3: Why are HP, Dell and Apple not instant?
a3: HP, Dell and Apple protect their warranty data with a captcha or bot protection. Warranty Check confirms the HP model and opens the right HP, Dell or Apple page for you, with the serial ready to paste.
q4: Is it free? Is my serial number stored?
a4: It is free, with no account. The serial is only sent to the manufacturer to look up the warranty. Your recent checks are saved in your own browser, never on a server.
q5: Is it useful when buying a used laptop?
a5: Yes. Before buying a second-hand or refurbished laptop, check the serial to see if the warranty is still valid, when it ends, and the exact model, so you know what you are paying for.
dellNote: Dell only shows warranty dates on its own site. The Express Service Code is what Dell support asks for on the phone.
appleNote: Apple shows coverage after a captcha. The serial is copied when you open it: paste it with Ctrl+V.
appleRandom: Since 2021 Apple serials are random, so the model can't be read from them.
